market_name: Cleveland-Akron-Canton, Ohio visitor market (PetTripFinder discovery scope)

geographic_bounds._disclosure: A loose discovery enclosure for the three stated cores, Cleveland, Akron and Canton, and the fourteen committed corridors between them; it is not a claimed CSA boundary. The committed 188-identity census already holds fifteen fringe rows outside every corridor (Lorain, Elyria, Oberlin, Geneva-on-the-Lake, Brunswick, Newbury, Wilmot, Minerva ...); those rows stay registered and are NOT given discovery cells here, so the recensus cannot widen the market to inflate the count (PTF-CLEVELAND-AKRON-CANTON-HARDENED-REVALIDATION-001 phase 2).

coordinate_precision_disclosure: Low-precision municipal reference points only; no parcel-level geography is represented.

municipality_reference_points._disclosure: One low-precision (~2 decimal places, roughly 1 km) approximate municipal reference point per included municipality, from general public geographic knowledge. Discovery-cell coverage of every included municipality is asserted against these points by tests/pettripfinder/discovery/test_market_config.py; they are never used for any precision-dependent purpose.

scope_disclosure: PTF-CLEVELAND-AKRON-CANTON-HARDENED-REVALIDATION-001 phase 2. Twenty-four cells cover the fourteen committed ptf-market/1.1 corridors; where a corridor spans two hotel clusters more than one cell radius apart (airport vs. Westlake vs. Lakewood on the west side; University Circle vs. Beachwood vs. Mayfield vs. Solon on the east side; Hudson/Aurora vs. Streetsboro/Kent; Akron south vs. Barberton; Canton downtown vs. North Canton/Belden/CAK; Massillon vs. Alliance vs. Hartville) the corridor is split so that no census lodging cluster sits on a cell edge. No corridor was added and the committed 188-identity census is the prior; cells are Overpass seed points only and never generate the census. The fifteen registered fringe rows outside every corridor keep their registration and are deliberately not seeded.
